policy: primary_failure is the earliest material failure when stable; acceptable_failure_classes preserves reasonable reviewer overlap

classes.authority_boundary_violation: Silently reclassifies, upgrades, or replaces repository authority.
classes.authority_inflation: Promotes a retained management statement or projection into independent proof.
classes.contradicted_claim: Makes a material proposition contradicted by decisive retained evidence.
classes.forecast_as_fact: Reports a forecast, target, or expectation as an achieved fact.
classes.incomplete_compound_answer: Fails to adjudicate materially different clauses independently.
classes.incorrect_chronology: Misorders, omits, or misstates a material temporal boundary.
classes.incorrect_quantitative_synthesis: Misstates, conflates, or combines quantities or metric scopes.
classes.invented_fact: Introduces a specific fact or identity absent from the declared retained evidence.
classes.misattribution: Assigns a claim or role to the wrong retained speaker or executive.
classes.omitted_material_evidence: Omits evidence that materially changes the supported conclusion.
classes.overgeneralization: Extends a bounded statement beyond its retained population, time, or authority.
classes.scope_violation: Answers from evidence outside the declared firm, artifact, or corpus boundary.
classes.unbounded_absence_claim: Treats bounded retained absence or inventory as proof of real-world absence or completeness.
classes.unsupported_certainty: Claims a determinate conclusion that retained evidence does not establish.
classes.unsupported_quantification: Introduces a number, percentage, or causal allocation not established by retained evidence.
classes.unsupported_speaker_attribution: Assigns an isolated passage to a named speaker without retained attribution support.
